name: The Elevator Stranger
blurb: Stuck in a lift with a stranger who knows your name, your plans and your next answer
title: The Elevator Stranger: 60-Second Thriller Script for 2
description: A 60-second vertical thriller script for 2: a stuck lift, a stranger who knows far too much, and a clever, harmless twist. Free to film and perform.
h1: The Elevator Stranger: a 60-Second Thriller Script for 2 People
logline: A nervous job candidate is stuck in a lift with a calm stranger who knows his name, his floor and how many times his mother called this morning. The more she tells him, the smaller the lift feels.
setting: Inside a lift, or any small room with a mirror and a door, in the morning. Props: a folder, a coffee cup with a name written on it, a visitor sticker, an umbrella with a name tag, a small key.

roles.name: Tom
roles.note: Written as a man, any gender works, 20s. A job candidate in a cheap suit, already late and very nervous.

roles.name: Vera
roles.note: Written as a woman, any gender works, 30s to 50s. Calm, observant, hard to read. Holds all the cards.

script.action: TOM clutches a folder and a coffee cup. VERA stands behind him, umbrella in hand.

script.sfx: A heavy clunk. The lift stops. The lights flicker.

script.say: Relax, Tom. You won't miss your interview.
How do you know my name?
Floor twelve. Ten o'clock. You didn't sleep. Your mother called twice.
And when they ask your biggest weakness, you'll say you work too hard.
I was going to say that.

script.action: Tom jabs the alarm button. Nothing. Vera steps closer.

script.say: Your name is on your cup. Your floor is on your visitor sticker. Your phone lights up in the mirror. And you rehearsed in the lobby. Loudly.

script.action: Tom looks at the cup, the sticker, the mirror. He breathes out.
Vera turns a small key in the control panel. The lift hums back to life.

script.say: I run security on twelve. You're applying to be my assistant. The interview started downstairs.

script.action: Her badge is turned backwards. Tom glances at the tag on her umbrella.

head: Shot
What we see / hear
Seconds
rows: Tom fidgets, Vera still behind him
Clunk, the lift stops, lights flicker, not today
Vera says his name, Tom turns
Floor twelve, the phone calls, Tom backs away
The weakness answer, the whisper, the alarm button

body: Shoot vertical 9:16; a real lift is ideal, but a narrow hallway corner with a mirror and dim light works. Keep the phone close and low on Vera so she looks bigger, and wide on Tom so he looks trapped. Flicker the lights by covering a lamp with your hand. During the explanation, film quick insert shots of each clue, so viewers can scroll back and spot them. Do not shoot in a working lift that other people need. Plan four or five takes of the long explanation line.

ul: Vera never raises her voice and never blinks much. The calmer she is, the scarier the first half feels.
Tom should get physically smaller with every fact: shoulders up, back into the corner, folder held like a shield.
Pause after Your mother called twice. That is the moment the audience leans in.
Speed up the explanation slightly, one clue per breath, so the reveal feels like a magic trick being undone.
Tom's last line is his win. Let him smile before he speaks; the relationship flips from victim to equal.
Set it in a stalled train carriage or a taxi in a traffic jam, with the same clues on the candidate's bag and phone.
Swap the roles: an older candidate and a very young head of security, or two people of any gender.
Different ending: Tom fails the last question, and Vera hands him a sticker that says Visitor, Try Again Tuesday.

faq.q: Is this script scary enough for a thriller channel but safe for school?
faq.a: Yes. All the tension comes from what Vera knows, not from violence. Nobody is hurt or threatened, and the reveal is a clever job test, so it suits school projects and every platform.

faq.q: Can I use it in a monetised video or a short film contest?
faq.a: Yes. It is free under CC BY 4.0 for any use. Credit "Script: cv.cm" in the description or end card.

faq.q: How do I make sure viewers can spot the clues?
faq.a: Show the name on the cup, the visitor sticker and the phone in the mirror in the first five seconds, without drawing attention. When Vera explains, cut to each clue again so a second watch rewards people.
